title: Lesson 12: Speaking and Listening: Preparing for the End of Module Celebration
objective: Students will prepare to present information about the sun, moon, and stars by selecting notebook entries, discussing learned patterns, and practicing reading their writing aloud with clarity and confidence.

what_is_taught.skill: present information about the sun, moon, and stars to others
select notebook entries based on neat writing, accurate information, and variety of times of day
discuss patterns and information about the sun, moon, and stars with a partner using a structured protocol
practice reading writing aloud using a strong and clear voice
use complete sentences when presenting information
follow presentation guidelines such as speaking clearly, using a loud voice, and making eye contact
respond to questions about the sun, moon, and stars

evidence.quote: I can present information about the sun, moon, and stars to others.
'What work have you done during this module that you could share with visitors so that they learn about the sun, moon, and stars?' (Sky notebook, 'What the Sun Sees' poem)
Direct students' attention to the Ways We Share Our Work anchor chart and briefly review it by reading it aloud, inviting students to echo you:
Tell students that they will now review their Sky notebooks and pick two entries to share with the visitors.
Using a total participation technique, invite responses from the group:

Think aloud as you reflect on the quality of information and writing included on this page. (Example: 'This entry is about the sun at noontime. I drew a really detailed picture and picked two adjectives to describe what the sun looks like.)
Tell students they will use the sticky notes to mark the two entries they will share with visitors during the end of module celebration.
Circulate as students review their notebooks, prompting them to select entries with show neat writing, accurate information, and different times of day.

Invite students back to the whole group area and offer them specific, positive feedback on their work selecting entries from their Sky notebooks. (Example: 'I noticed that everyone reviewed their work closely to select the entries that had the most details to describe the sun or moon.')
Tell students that the visitors will ask them a few questions about the sun, moon, and stars and that they will now practice answering those questions with a partner.

Tell students they are going to use the Back-to-Back and Face-to-Face protocol to discuss the answers to questions about the sun, moon, and stars and what they have learned. Remind them that they used this protocol in previous lessons and review as necessary using the Back-to-Back and Face-to-Face Protocol anchor chart. (Refer to the Classroom Protocols document for the full version of the protocol.)
Guide students through four rounds of the protocol using the following questions:
Invite a few students to share out what they discussed with their partners during the protocol.
Tell students that they have one more piece of work to share with their visitors: their 'What the Sun Sees' poems.
I can read my writing aloud using a strong and clear voice.
'When you are sharing your poems, what is important to remember to do so that your visitors can learn from you?' (speak clearly and loudly, make eye contact with visitors, listen as others share)
Tell students that they will now practice sharing their poems with a partner so that they are prepared to share them when the visitors come.
Invite students to begin the Pinky Partners protocol.
Circulate as students share, directing students' attention to the Ways We Share Our Work anchor chart as necessary and making note of progress toward using the Speaking and Listening Checklist.
'What part of your poem are you most proud and most excited to share with a visitor?' (Responses will vary.)

Tell students that in addition to sharing their Sky notebooks and 'What the Sun Sees' poems with visitors, they will also share the 'Sun' song and 'Moon' song they had practiced and learned during Unit 1.
Direct students' attention to the posted 'Sun, Moon, and Stars' song.
Invite students to join you as you sing the song and complete the accompanying hand motions.

'How did our work in this unit add to your understanding of how writers use their knowledge and observations to write a story? I'll give you time to think and discuss with a partner.' (Responses will vary.)

Invite students to be seated and offer specific, positive feedback on all that they did during today's lesson to prepare for the celebration in the next lesson. (Example: 'When we sing for the visitors, we want to make sure we are looking at the audience so they can hear the songs clearly.')

teacher_actions.direct_instruction: Model selecting notebook entries based on neat writing, accurate information, and variety of times of day; model using sticky notes to mark selected entries; model using Back-to-Back and Face-to-Face and Pinky Partners speaking protocols; model reading learning targets aloud; model singing the 'Sun, Moon, and Stars' song with hand motions; provide specific positive feedback on student work and presentation preparation.
prompts_that_cue_student_response: What work have you done during this module that you could share with visitors so that they learn about the sun, moon, and stars?
What should you keep in mind while you are selecting entries from your Sky notebook to share? What criteria should those entries meet?
What is a pattern that the sun, moon, or stars follow? How would you describe that pattern?
What is something you learned about the sun, moon, or stars that you did not know before?
What do you still wonder about the sun, moon, or stars?
What did you learn about the Unit 3 guiding question: How do writers use their knowledge and observations to write a story?
When you are sharing your poems, what is important to remember to do so that your visitors can learn from you?
What part of your poem are you most proud and most excited to share with a visitor?
How did our work in this unit add to your understanding of how writers use their knowledge and observations to write a story?

scope.breadth: selecting and sharing information about the sun, moon, and stars; practicing oral presentation skills; discussing learned content and patterns; preparing for a celebration presentation
scope.depth: applying criteria to select notebook entries; using structured speaking protocols to discuss and share information; practicing clear and confident oral reading

context.stimulus_provided: listening to teacher read learning targets and anchor charts; reviewing own notebook entries and poems; partner discussions; singing songs

sections_covered.warm_up: Engaging the Learner: Ways We Share Our Work Anchor Chart
sections_covered.direct_instruction: Model selecting notebook entries and using speaking protocols
sections_covered.guided_practice: Partner discussions using Back-to-Back and Face-to-Face and Pinky Partners protocols
sections_covered.independent_application: Selecting notebook entries; practicing poem sharing with a partner
sections_covered.check_for_understanding: Student sharing out partner discussions and poem parts they are proud of
sections_covered.differentiated_reinforce: Providing wait time and pairing ELLs with buddies or strategic partners
sections_covered.differentiated_extend: Encouraging students to practice reading the anchor chart at home and preparing scripts for the celebration

supports.english_language_learners: Provide wait time; pair ELLs with buddies or strategic partners; send home anchor chart and scripts for practice; clarify visitor identities and presentation group sizes
supports.universal_design_udl: Use total participation techniques; provide visual timers and clear routines; use anchor charts and protocols; provide positive, specific feedback
supports.below_level_reinforce: Use High-Quality Work anchor chart to support selection of notebook entries; allow students to choose questions to answer during partner discussions
supports.above_level_extend: Encourage students to practice reading scripts aloud at home; invite volunteers to read anchor charts during the celebration

assessment.method: Observation of student participation in partner discussions, notebook entry selection, poem sharing, and oral responses during class discussions and protocols

materials: Ways We Share Our Work anchor chart (begun in Module 1)
Sky notebook (from Unit 2, Lesson 4; answers, for teacher reference; one to display)
Sky notebooks (completed in Unit 2; one per student)
Back-to-Back and Face-to-Face Protocol anchor chart (begun in Module 1)
Speaking and Listening Checklist (for teacher reference; see Assessment Overview and Resources)
Equity sticks (class set; one per student)
Pinky Partners Protocol anchor chart (begun in Module 1)
'What the Sun Sees' poem (completed in Lesson 11; one per student)
'Sun, Moon, and Stars' song (from Unit 1, Lesson 3; one to display)
'Moon' song (from Unit 1, Lesson 8; one to display)
notes: This lesson prepares students for an end-of-module celebration where they will present their knowledge about the sun, moon, and stars. It emphasizes oral presentation skills, partner discussion protocols, and selection of quality notebook entries to share. Supports for ELLs and students needing additional oral language practice are included.

text_complexity.quantitative: Read-aloud mediation; no independent decoding required
text_complexity.qualitative: Simple structure with familiar language and concepts about the sun, moon, and stars; low knowledge demands due to prior unit work
text_complexity.reader_and_task: Students engage with their own writing and partner discussions; tasks scaffolded with protocols and anchor charts
